 JUDGMENT
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 04.12.2022.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 04.12.2022 at about 12.30pm the petitioner was proceeding in his brother's motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02- JZ-8886 as a pillion rider from Nelamangala to Tavarekere Main Road to go to his village, when they reached near Jettipalya Village, Tavarekere - Nelamangala Main Road, a Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-42-8104 and KA-42-8105 came from opposite side i.e., from Tavarekere, driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to Kenganahalli Hospital, Nice Road, provided first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Nandini Layout, Bangalore, admitted as an inpatient, underwent surgeries and discharged with advice.

food and nourishment SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.411/2023 etc.,
At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, working as a Labor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, he became disabled and could not work as before the accident.
He lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-42-8104 & KA-42-8105.
The Tavarekere Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.395/2022.
Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2 nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.

4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
5.

The objection of the respondent No.1.
SCCH - 25 5 MVC No.411/2023 She has admitted that the Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-42-8104 & KA-42-8105 was insured with the 2nd respondent but denied the involvement of the vehicle and rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing No.KA-42-8104 & KA-42-8105 in the accident.
The accident caused due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JZ-8886.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. The objection of the respondent No.2.
It has denied all the averments made in the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the Tractor and Trailer bearing KA-42-8104 & KA-42-8105.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
There was 6 days delay in filing the FIR.
Further contended that the accident was caused due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself.
The petition is also bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
The driver of the Tractor and Trailer did not have valid SCCH - 25 6 MVC No.411/2023 and effective DL as on the date of accident.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.

Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
7.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 04.12.2022 at about 12.30pm, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-42-8104 & KA-42-8105 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries.?
2. Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?

On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

Further there is delay of 5 days in filing the FIR.

sentences.text: He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind,
Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Kenganar Hospital, Nice Road and thereafter shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 07.12.2022 to 17.12.2022 and from 05.01.2023 to 07.01.2023 and was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.9.

Considering that SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.411/2023 the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for a sum of Rs.8,29,393/-.
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Three months time for recovering from the injuries sustained SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.411/2023 by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.46,500/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.12 as well as Affidavit, the petitioner's age is mentioned as 28 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 28 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 17.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.7,90,500/-
(Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 17 x 25%= Rs.7,90,500/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 28 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 25% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age and SCCH - 25 17 MVC No.411/2023 nature of injuries Basavaraja vs Bharathi.M on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18566678/
7 that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 8,29,393/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.46,500/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.7,90,500/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.17,86,393/-
SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.411/2023
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.17,86,400/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Liability 19.
The Respondents have contended that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.17,86,400/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.

The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Three months time for recovering from the injuries sustained SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.411/2023 by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.46,500/- under this head.
The Respondents have contended that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

18. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 8,29,393/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.46,500/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.7,90,500/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.17,86,393/-
SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.411/2023
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.17,86,400/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.30,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.17,86,400/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.17,86,400/- (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Eighty Six Thousand and Four Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
SCCH - 25 20 MVC No.411/2023 On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any N/S Bank and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
